# Smart Money Frontend - Business Logic Reference (llms.txt)

Overview
- The system is a consumer-facing financial app focused on budgeting, spending analytics, and secure account management. It orchestrates authentication and onboarding, tabbed navigation, transaction workflows (including receipts and media), project/budget management, and analytics with real-time and AI-assisted capabilities.
- Core guarantee: consistent business flows across authenticated surfaces, with extensible data contracts and UI theming.

Data model overview and relationships
- User and authentication
  - Auth surface governs login, signup, OTP, social logins, password reset.
  - Key contracts: auth/types define UserState, UserResponse, tokens, and multipart payloads (RegisterRequest -> FormData).
  - Token storage underpins the session boundary between client and backend.
- Projects (budget/portfolio)
  - Types define PERSONAL vs GROUP projects, with create/update payloads and contributor management.
  - Project utilities compute currency formatting, deadlines, progress, and filtering; support for invitations and contributions.
  - Project list/detail shapes drive multi-view budgeting/reporting.
  - A personal project that belongs to a group project carries a groupProjectId on its detail; this marks it as a "sub-personal" project and changes its lifecycle controls (abandon-then-delete instead of direct delete).
- Groups and group projects (collaborative saving)
  - Types in group.types.ts model groups, members, invites, and group projects (GroupDetailResponse, GroupMemberResponse, GroupProjectDetailResponse, GroupProjectMemberDetail, and suggestion/create/join payloads).
  - Group lifecycle: FORMING (admin invites members) -> LOCKED (admin manually locks once at least one member has joined) -> DISSOLVED. Locking gates group-project creation.
  - Group project creation is admin-only, allowed only on days 1-7 of the month (date gate, bypassable in dev via EXPO_PUBLIC_BYPASS_DATE_GATE); target amount and deadline are fixed after creation. A two-way suggestions calculator estimates by target amount or by months from members' combined monthly capacity.
  - Members join a group project by picking a unique priority (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), which spins up their sub-personal project; each member has at most one sub-project per group project.
  - Per-member sub-project status is ACTIVE | FROZEN | COMPLETED | ABANDONED; abandoned rows are de-emphasized (blurred) in the group-project detail. Member identities display username with a userId fallback; per-member monetary capacity is intentionally hidden from everyone, including the admin.
  - API surface (group.api.ts): create/list/detail groups, invite/accept/decline/remove members, lock group, group-project suggestions/create/detail, join, and dissolve. group.api.ts and groupStorage.ts provide local fallbacks (known group IDs, groupId -> groupProjectId map) for fields the backend may not yet return.
- Transactions
  - Transactions are EXPENSE or INCOME, with create/update, and list queries.
  - Attach receipts (media assets) via cloud storage and receipts API.
  - Category picker and date-range filtering shape analytics and reporting.
  - Supporting types include TransactionQuery, TransactionListResponse, TransactionDateRange, Receipt.
- Receipts and media
  - Cloudinary contracts model receipt/image upload lifecycle and payloads (SaveReceiptPayload, ReceiptResponse).
  - Media ingest supports receipts linked to transactions.
- Analytics
  - Analytics contracts (AnalyticsRequest/Data/Response) support time-series and category breakdowns for transactions.
  - UI surfaces analytics over time (monthly trends, category proportions).
- Notifications
  - Push tokens, notification entities, and create/list operations drive in-app alerts and toasts.
  - Notification service, listener, and native bridge handle delivery and UI feedback.
  - Notification state persisted in storage for consistency across sessions.
- AI integration
  - AI job response type (AIJobResponse) models results from asynchronous AI processing feeding into workflows (analyses, recommendations, enrichment).
- Theme and internationalization
  - Theming is two-tier: ThemeProvider exposes ThemeMode ("light" | "dark"); useThemeMode reads mode; tokens.ts defines per-mode Theme palettes.
  - i18n provides translations (en/vi) with LanguageProvider controlling locale.
- Core utilities and contracts
  - dateFormatter.ts governs display and parsing formats.
  - transactionParser.ts converts raw event data into UI-friendly transactions.
  - Validation contracts enforce client-side checks for forms (auth_login validation).

Key end-to-end workflows (high level)
- User onboarding and authentication
  - User arrives at intro screens, proceeds to auth surface, chooses login or signup, optionally uses social login.
  - OTP verification and RememberMe decisions drive session persistence; upon success, user lands in the main tabbed UI.
- Main app navigation and surfaces
  - Post-auth, a root layout renders authentication-, onboarding-, and main-tab chrome; Tab navigation routes to Home, Analytics, Transactions, Profile.
- Transactions lifecycle
  - Create: user opens AddTransactionModal, enters amount/date/category/type; optionally attaches a receipt (Cloudinary) or a voice/note; submit persists via transaction API.
  - Read/Review: list view groups transactions by sections (TransactionSection); detail view opens for edits or deletes via EditTransactionModal.
  - Media flow: receipts flow through camera or upload, preview, and final association.
- Projects, groups, and collaborative saving
  - Personal project: created via a multi-step modal where a saving-plan advisor (ProjectAPI.advisor -> /projects/project-advisor) suggests a monthly contribution and duration for the chosen mode; the project tab toggles between Personal and Group lists.
  - Group flow: an admin creates a group, invites members by email (deep-link accept/decline), and manually locks it once members have joined. From a locked group the admin opens the suggestions calculator and creates a group project (days 1-7 only).
  - Join flow: a joined member opens the group project, picks an unused priority, and the backend creates their sub-personal project mirroring the group target.
  - Teardown: an individual member abandons their own sub-personal project first (status -> ABANDONED), after which a delete becomes available; an admin can dissolve the whole group project, which also removes every member's sub-personal project.
- Receipts and media management
  - Images/receipts uploaded to Cloudinary; SaveReceiptPayload persists linkage to the corresponding transaction and asset metadata.
- Analytics and insights
  - Analytics API fetches time-series (monthly) and category breakdowns; frontend derives recent months for display and renders charts.
- Notifications and real-time updates
  - Push token registration enables delivery; notification service funnels events to toasts or in-app banners; WebSocket service delivers real-time hooks for active sessions.
- Preferences and settings
  - Profile and Settings surface enable sign-out, privacy/security, preferences (language, theme), and notification controls; language toggles affect translations globally.

Primary external dependencies and what they’re used for
- Backend API and HTTP client
  - src/api/* and http.ts provide service calls for auth, transactions, receipts, projects, analytics, and notifications.
- Supabase backend binding
  - lib/supabase.ts underpins auth, data storage, and real-time capabilities.
- Cloud storage for media
  - cloudinary.api.ts and cloudinary.service.ts handle image/receipt uploads and asset management.
- Push notifications and native bridges
  - Notification-related modules, registerForPushNotificationsAsync.ts, and NotificationNative.ts manage device tokens and delivery.
- WebSocket and real-time
  - websocket.ts and aiWebSocketHelper.ts enable persistent connections and async AI/result streaming.
- AI services
  - src/api/ai.api.ts and ai.types.ts model AI-driven tasks and their typed responses.
- Internationalization and theming
  - i18n/index.ts, LanguageProvider.tsx, tokens.ts, ThemeProvider.tsx govern language and theme tokens; ThemeMode drives light/dark palettes.
- Assets, inputs, and validation
  - Components like InputField.tsx, SignInForm.tsx, SignUpForm.tsx, and validation.ts support user entry, validation feedback, and UX safety.

Dominant architectural patterns
- Layered, modular frontend
  - Clear separation of UI (screens/components), domain logic (types, hooks), and data (API/services, storage).
- Event-driven UI feedback
  - Global notificationEmitter enables decoupled cross-component signaling for alerts and status changes.
- State and context orchestration
  - AuthContext, OnboardingContext, NotificationUIContext centralize state and behavior across screens.
- Real-time and asynchronous flows
  - WebSocket and AI/WebSocket helpers coordinate live updates and AI-augmented steps within flows (e.g., waiting for AI results).
- Theming and localization
  - Two-tier theming with runtime mode switching and token-based palettes ensure consistent visuals and translations.

Notes on data contracts and boundaries
- Data contracts (auth.types.ts, project.types.ts, group.types.ts, transaction.types.ts, notification.type.ts, cloudinary.types.ts, ai.types.ts) codify the shapes of payloads, API responses, and UI-facing structures.
- The system enforces boundaries between UI forms, backend payloads, and storage/state, enabling predictable naming, validation, and error handling across modules.

This document aggregates the business logic surface from authentication, onboarding, tabbed navigation, transactions with media, analytics, projects, and notification systems, emphasizing end-to-end workflows, data contracts, external dependencies, and architectural patterns for a cohesive llms.txt reference.
